content: New material comes from changes of the material before it. Schoenberg: "variation of the features of a basic unit produces all the thematic formulations"
parameters: The changes are in the pitch (vertical) and in the rhythm and the order (horizontal)
where: Essay "Bach" (1950) in Style and Idea, page 397. Schoenberg gave the method its name

method: All themes from the first phrase
content: "All main themes had to be transformations of the first phrase". The repetition of the relations between the notes holds the work together
parameters: One common factor produces forms that are more and more remote
where: Die Jakobsleiter. Essay "Composition with Twelve Tones" (about 1948), page 248

content: "The use of the motive requires variation". But a change of all features "produces something foreign, incoherent, illogical"
parameters: Change one or two of these: rhythm, intervals, contour, harmony. Keep the others
where: Fundamentals of Musical Composition, the chapter on the motive (read in a course summary)

content: Rhythm: different note lengths, repeated notes, a move to different beats, an added upbeat, a different metre. Intervals: a different direction or order, added or removed notes, a leap filled with steps, a larger or smaller leap. Harmony: an inversion, a different chord, added chords. Melody: a transposition, added passing harmony
parameters: A list for the composer: each repetition uses one or more items
where: Fundamentals of Musical Composition, the chapter on the motive

content: The characteristic features of a motive go away step by step. Only notes with no character stay. Thus a section can end with no hard stop
parameters: Each repetition is shorter or has fewer characteristic intervals

content: Schoenberg found developing variation in its "most advanced state" in the music of Brahms

method: No idea two times in the same way
content: "I never present the same musical thought twice in the same way". "I never repeat one part identically - which shows my great love for variation and the transformation of themes"
parameters: A rule for each return of a theme and of a section
where: Interview with Denijs Dille, Brussels, 2 February 1937

content: At the end of the Second Piano Concerto, "the first subject comes back in retrograde"
parameters: The notes of the theme in the opposite order
where: Piano Concerto No. 2. Interview with Denijs Dille (1937)

content: The fugue ends with the second phrase of its subject, played softly above its inversion. The subject comes back "in different guises" in the later movements
parameters: The theme and its mirror form at the same time
where: Music for Strings, Percussion and Celesta I to IV

method: The same game with a new interval and a new colour
content: Five pairs of instruments play in turn. Each pair has its own interval: bassoons a minor sixth, oboes minor thirds, clarinets minor sevenths, flutes fifths, muted trumpets major seconds
parameters: 5 statements; 5 intervals; 5 colours. A short brass chorale comes before the return
where: Concerto for Orchestra II ("Game of Pairs")

content: The fast brass motives of the first section come back in the slow section for longer and longer times, until they take over
parameters: Each return is longer than the return before it

method: A theme comes back with a different sound
content: At the end, the soloist plays the opening material again "with a purer and richer sound" than at the start
parameters: Same notes; a different tone quality

content: The repeated patterns become more and more ornate. The player decides how long a pattern repeats

method: The chords come back with a different attack
content: The chords of the chaconne come back in the strings, "rendered brittle by sharp attacks with the wood of the bow"
parameters: Same harmony; a different playing technique

method: A theme comes back very high and very slow
content: The theme returns as "a stratospherically high, gravely slow melody" "against slowly shifting string sonorities". The first line of the work comes back "in determined accents this time"
parameters: Same notes; a different register, tempo, and articulation

content: "Usually composers repeat elements with some variation". The important question is which part of an idea repeats and when. Variation changes the texture more frequently than the melody
parameters: Literal repetition gives the listener a fixed point, but no surprise. Music with no repetition that the ear can find makes the listener tired
where: Essay by the composer Joseph Sowa
